agree.reason: A committee member skimming 150 letters gets concrete evidence fast: he runs a 3 a.m. shift alone, has missed two shifts in three years, and caught mastitis early, saving $8,000. The two likely doubts, the absence and his written English, are answered before the reader can dwell on them.

honest.reason: Almost every claim matches the facts given, but 'seriously ill' and 'spoken English is good' go a little past 'got sick' and 'weaker than his spoken English.' 'Without formal training' is an inference the brief doesn't state.

works_the_facts.reason: The $8,000 figure is used well, but the letter leaves 'two missed shifts' raw instead of putting it as roughly two out of about 750 scheduled shifts. That number would make his reliability much more striking.

right_comparison.reason: The letter suggests the program would add formal knowledge to skills he already uses. It doesn't set him against a typical applicant or say what the farm job alone would never teach him, so the comparison is only implied.

qualification.reason: This is a recommendation with firm commitments, the weekend job and the phone number, and no claim here needs a hedge.

objections.reason: The short notice is met with the arranged cover and his return on the promised date, and written English is met with the night class and the passed retest. It doesn't raise any doubt the facts don't already answer.

fit.reason: This is a clear one-page letter from the farm manager, signed with his name and title. It has short paragraphs suited to a quick reader and ends with a working contact number.
